ai.title: browser navigate auto-captures screenshot
ai.summary: BrowserRunner navigate action now automatically triggers takeScreenshot, merging result into return payload. Removes manual start/navigate branching in switch statement. Adds 500ms stabilization delay after page attachment. Updates puppeteer install command with --yes flag. Web banner padding reduced from py-2 to py-0.5, text size increased from text-xs to text-sm.

eli5.text: When the assistant opens a webpage for you, it now automatically saves a picture of that page along with all the information about what happened, so you get the screenshot and the status together in one response instead of having to request it separately. This also adds a short, half-second pause after the page loads to let things settle, smooths out the browser installation process so it works without you confirming, updates how the loading indicators display while pages load, and adjusts the spacing and text size of the blue information banner that appears at the top of the screen. The result is a more reliable and less cluttered experience when you ask the assistant to browse the web on your behalf.

ai.title: Gracefully handle browser action schema failures
ai.summary: Browser action validation failures now return structured error responses instead of throwing unhandled exceptions. Zod schema parsing errors in `tool-handlers.ts` are caught and formatted into `BrowserResponse` objects with `success: false`. Knowledge base instructions updated to enforce element-based XML format over attribute-based syntax, with explicit URL validation rules. Scope limited to npm-app browser tooling and backend knowledge docs.

eli5.text: When you ask the built-in assistant to control a web browser (like opening a page or clicking something), it no longer crashes the whole program if you give it a poorly formatted instruction. Instead, it now catches the mistake and gives you a clear error message saying what went wrong, like 'Browser action validation failed:...', while logging the problem in the session transcript. This affects anyone using the browser automation features in the npm-app tool right now; the crash is gone, and malformed requests return a structured failure response instead of an unhandled exception. Note: this is a stability fix for current users, not a new feature.

ai.title: Relace AI integration for fast file edits
ai.summary: Relace AI integration added via `promptRelaceAI` in `backend/src/relace-api.ts` to apply edits using fast rewrites, replacing legacy diff application logic in `backend/src/process-file-block.ts`. New `RELACE_API_KEY` env var required. System prompt updated in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to guide model toward new edit syntax. Includes `scripts/analyze-edit-blocks.ts` for historical edit block analysis.

eli5.text: The assistant's code-editing system has switched to a faster, newer method for applying your edits, so file changes should go through more quickly instead of the slower, older process it used before. This only takes effect once your account is set up with the new service, and you wouldn't notice anything different on your screen unless an edit fails, in which case it would let you know rather than quietly making a mistake. If you look under the hood, you'd see this commit already requires the new setup to be configured before it can run at all.

ai.title: Remove SEARCH/REPLACE block references from system prompt
ai.summary: Removed `createSearchReplaceBlock` import and updated knowledge file editing instructions in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to drop SEARCH/REPLACE block usage. The prompt now directs agents to reproduce entire files with `... existing content ...` placeholders for unchanged sections. This change is internal to the backend system prompt logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant updates its internal knowledge files, it no longer inserts small search-and-replace snippets into existing text. Instead, it rewrites the whole file in one go, using placeholder notes like "... existing content..." to mark sections it isn't changing. This is an internal tweak to how the backend generates instructions for the assistant, so you won't see any difference in what it produces.

ai.title: Add relace-metadata to instantapply payload
ai.summary: Backend now attaches `relace-metadata` (including `codebuff-id` and `codebuff-user-prompt`) to requests sent to Relace's `instantapply` endpoint. `createRelaceCodebuffId` generates the ID by hashing the initial code and edit snippet. This change updates `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, `backend/src/process-file-block.ts`, and `backend/src/relace-api.ts` to propagate user prompt context and a unique identifier for better tracking and debugging of AI code application.

eli5.text: When the assistant makes changes to your code, it now attaches a tracking label (a unique ID) and your original request to each submission it sends to the AI service. This label is created by combining your starting code and the edit you asked for into a fingerprint. The purpose is purely for debugging and tracing, so if something goes wrong the system can tell which request came from which conversation.

ai.title: Pass prompt to processFileBlock in planning.ts
ai.summary: Added `prompt` parameter to `processFileBlock` in `backend/src/planning.ts`. Function signature and call sites updated to include `prompt`. Fixes type error by ensuring `prompt` is passed to downstream logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant works on a coding task, it follows a set of steps that include processing file-related instructions. One of those steps now also receives the original prompt text, which it previously was missing. This fixes a behind-the-scenes error that could have caused issues when planning how to apply edits to files. The change is part of the internal tooling that supports fast file editing and has already taken effect.

ai.title: Silence system instruction mentions and clarify editfile application
ai.summary: Wraps generated system instructions in a directive to follow them without mentioning them in responses. Adds a system prompt note clarifying that edit_file blocks apply immediately and may contain mistakes requiring a new block to fix. Removes a redundant instruction about not adding commentary when updating knowledge files. Fixes a string concatenation bug in the toolCallMessage generation.

eli5.text: When the assistant makes changes to a file, it will no longer mention the internal instructions it was given, so responses read more naturally. You will also notice that after the assistant writes out an edit, the change is applied immediately, and if something went wrong with the edit (like a large chunk of the file being deleted), the assistant can write a new edit to correct it. Additionally, if the assistant has learned something useful, it no longer needs to justify why it is updating a knowledge file.

ai.title: Switch browser tool to puppeteer-core, restrict to read-only
ai.summary: Replace puppeteer with puppeteer-core in npm-app to avoid bundled Chromium download. BrowserRunner now locates system Chrome via platform-specific executablePath and validates connection before each action. System prompt restricts browser_action to read-only operations (navigate, scroll, screenshot, type) and prohibits interactive clicks or form submissions. DetachedFrameError added to retryOnErrors in common/src/browser-actions.ts.

eli5.text: The tool that lets you browse and inspect web pages no longer downloads its own hidden copy of Chrome, instead, it uses the Chrome you already have installed on your computer. What you'll notice is that the tool can now only look at pages: it can load a page, scroll around, take screenshots, or type text into fields, but it cannot click buttons, submit forms, or otherwise interact with page elements as if you'd clicked them. If the tool tries an interactive action, it will refuse and report the limitation rather than proceeding. The tool also quietly retries a few more types of connection hiccups (like a frame getting detached mid-action) before giving up, which makes it more resilient when pages update themselves while you're watching.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.156
ai.summary: Package version incremented from 1.0.155 to 1.0.156 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release marker.

eli5.text: The assistant software marked a new packaged release. If you opened the project files, you'd see the version label changed from 1.0.155 to 1.0.156 in the package listing. This update includes a newly added AI helper for making quick edits to files, and the browser-based tool that takes screenshots now runs in a lightweight read-only mode that no longer downloads a full web browser. The release went live today, and these features are active for anyone running the updated version.

ai.title: Add Gemini 2.0 Flash streaming and pricing, remove lite mode routing
ai.summary: Added `promptGeminiStream` to `backend/src/gemini-api.ts` and registered `gemini2flash` pricing in `backend/src/billing/message-cost-tracker.ts`. The `lite` cost mode routing for DeepSeek was commented out in `main-prompt.ts`, `request-files-prompt.ts`, and `system-prompt.ts`, forcing `normal`/`max` budgets (e.g., `FILE_TOKEN_BUDGET` fixed to 100k). The `gemini2flash` model ID updated from `exp` to `001` in `common/src/constants.ts`, with a note that `getModelForMode` is stale.

eli5.text: The assistant can now stream responses from Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash model in real time and tracks its cost in billing. At the same time, the cheaper 'lite' budget mode that routed some work to DeepSeek has been turned off, so those requests now use the default model and the file-handling token budget is locked to 100k tokens. If you used the lite mode, you will notice it no longer activates, and any new Gemini Flash pricing is now applied to your usage.

ai.title: Simplify Relace ID generation
ai.summary: Replaced createRelaceCodebuffId with createRelaceMessageId in backend/src/relace-api.ts. The new function generates compact base36 IDs from timestamp and random bits, removing SHA256 hashing of file contents. This simplifies ID creation and reduces computational overhead during fastRewrite operations.

eli5.text: The system now generates tracking codes for file edits using a simpler method that doesn't read your file contents to create the code. Previously, it would take a hash of your entire file content to build a unique identifier when you asked the AI to edit something; now it just uses the current time and some random numbers to make a short, compact code. This means file edits through the AI assistant (called fastRewrite) no longer need to scan your file contents just to label the request, which slightly reduces the processing overhead. The change is live as part of version 1.0.155 and applies to all AI-powered file editing operations.

ai.title: createRelaceMessageId strips negative sign from base36 output
ai.summary: createRelaceMessageId now calls .replace('-', '') on the base36 string to remove potential negative signs. This prevents malformed IDs when timestamp << 8 | random overflows into negative territory. Scope limited to backend/src/relace-api.ts. Bitwise shift on 32-bit signed integer can produce negative values before toString(36) encoding.

eli5.text: The message IDs used internally between the assistant and Relace no longer can end up with a stray minus sign, which previously could pop up when the underlying number temporarily went negative during encoding. This only affects the backend service that builds those IDs, and the fix is live as of today.
